::: {#thm-sqrt-two}
#### $\sqrt{2}$ is irrational

The square root of $2$ is irrational (@def-irrational-numbers)
[@wikipedia_square_root_of_2].

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Suppose, for contradiction, that $\sqrt{2}$ is rational (@def-rational-numbers).
Then $\sqrt{2} = \frac{a}{b}$ for some integers $a$ and $b$ with $b \ne 0$.
Since $\sqrt{2} > 0$, we can take $a$ and $b$ positive
(if $b < 0$, replace $a$ and $b$ with $-a$ and $-b$).
So the set of positive integers $b$ for which $\sqrt{2}\, b$ is an integer has an element,
and by @rem-well-ordering it has a smallest element.
Let $b$ be that smallest element, and let $a = \sqrt{2}\, b$, a positive integer.

By @sol-sqrt-bounds, $b < a < 2b$,
so $b' = a - b$ is an integer with $0 < b' < b$.
Let $a' = 2b - a$, also an integer. Then

$$
\ba
\sqrt{2}\, b'
&= \sqrt{2}\, (a - b)
&& \text{(definition of } b' \text{)}
\\&= \sqrt{2}\, a - \sqrt{2}\, b
&& \text{(distributive law)}
\\&= \sqrt{2}\, \sqrt{2}\, b - a
&& \text{(substitute } a = \sqrt{2}\, b \text{ in each term)}
\\&= 2b - a
&& \text{(} \sqrt{2}\, \sqrt{2} = 2 \text{)}
\\&= a'.
&& \text{(definition of } a' \text{)}
\ea
$$

So $b'$ is a positive integer for which $\sqrt{2}\, b'$ is an integer,
and $b' < b$.
That contradicts the choice of $b$ as the smallest such integer.
So $\sqrt{2}$ is not rational.

:::

:::
